Input checks and troubleshooting

troubleshooting.Rmd

Most problems are easier to solve when you separate the steps. First check that the inputs describe the same samples and ASVs. Then check whether the model has eligible data and the intended comparison. Only after that should you investigate plotting or export settings.

We recommend starting with a small subset whose contents you can inspect. An error message about missing identifiers, for example, is a reason to compare the identifiers rather than change the significance threshold. The checks below follow that order.

Find the step that needs attention

Table 1. Analysis inputs and options
Symptom Check
Missing columns or no sample overlap Inspect the contribution table header and compare its sample IDs to sample_names(ps). Use a stratified long table for SDAA.
Few eligible taxa or missing tree tips Compare contribution ASV IDs, taxonomy row names, and tree tip labels. Check rank assignments and whether you supplied a tree from the same ASVs.
TSS or AST fails Look for selected samples with zero total contribution in the individual taxon or function table. Also check whether the corresponding model retains enough features and samples.
No significant biomarkers Inspect the model and annotation messages, the group contrast, and the prespecified threshold. For taxon-oriented KEGG results, check KEGGREST availability and access to KEGG.
Chord reports no matching contrast or missing effects Compare group1 and group2 with the requested contrast. Use one method and contrast with finite signed effect estimates. The supplied limma voom and edgeR wrappers return p-values without signed effects.
Expected class names but see genus labels Check attr(result, "microfun")$taxon_level. If the fit was at genus level, refit at Class. For a legacy result without the attribute, pass the original rank explicitly to the plot.

Functional abundances and taxon contributions come from PICRUSt2 predictions. Interpret the plots together with the reference group, model, and adjustment scope recorded for the analysis.

What if no results are selected?

An empty result is not automatically a software failure. Read the model and annotation messages, check the contrast and confirm that enough samples and features remain. If those checks pass, the analysis may simply have no rows meeting the prespecified threshold. Changing the threshold after looking at a plot changes the question and should be documented.

KEGG annotation cannot connect

Confirm that KEGGREST is installed and that your R session can access the KEGG service. Academic REST access does not require an API key, so a connection error is not an instruction to register for one.

Local KO-to-pathway conversion can work while online annotation fails. A local kegg_map does not turn off the online annotation performed by the taxon-centered KO workflow. Check the annotation messages separately from model or sample-matching errors. The mapping and network access guide lists the local and online steps. The bundled community plotting examples use preannotated results and do not need a KEGG connection.

The plot looks different from what you expected

Begin with the quantity being shown. Sankey widths count associations, Chord widths show mean contributions, and signed bars show model coefficients. Boxplot group colours identify the groups, while ribbon colours identify effect direction. These choices can make two correct views look different.

Next compare the saved rank and selected cohort. A genus-level analysis and a class-level analysis are different aggregations; changing only the plot title cannot convert one into the other.

The analysis works, but the export fails

Check the export format and its optional dependencies. Tree Sankey PNG/PDF needs rsvg; tiled PDF also needs qpdf. Ordinary no-tree Sankey supports HTML and RDS. Chord SVG/HTML also needs a working SVG graphics device on your platform. Keep any adjacent HTML asset folders with the exported file.

If you ask for help, include the function call, the full error, a compact description of the input columns and sessionInfo(). A small reproducible example is more useful than a screenshot of the last line alone. Report issues through GitHub.
